 SCCH 15 3 MVC No.6459/2024  :JUDGMENT:
This petition emanates from the Motor Vehicle Accident dated 29.07.2024 wherein the petitioners have sought for compensation with respect to the death of Sri Eraswamy due to the impact of the accident.
2. Succinctly stated the facts germane to the lis involved in this petition are briefly summarized as follows:

It is the case of the petitioners that the petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioner No.2 and 3 are the sons and petitioner No.4 is the mother of the deceased Eraswamy who died in the Road Traffic Accident on 29.07.2024 due to the negligence of the rider of the respondent's vehicle.

It is submitted that on 29.07.2024 at about 5.00 p.m., deceased Eraswamy was proceeding in a motorcycle bearing Reg.KA-05-LV-8632 as a pillion rider and when they reached near Banana tree plantation, KM Doddi - Halaguru main road, at that time, rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.KA-05-LV-8632 (herein after referred to as offending vehicle) came in a rash and negligent manner and in SCCH 15 4 MVC No.6459/2024 the process of avoiding the cow which suddenly entered the road, lost control and turned to the left side, as result both rider and pillion rider fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately after the accident Eraswamy was shifted to Government hospital,
Malavalli and then shifted to Government hospital, Mandya, but doctor declared him as dead en route the hospital.

sentences.text: Consequently, on 30.07.2024 FIR No.0129/2024 was registered with the Halagur Police station under Sec.281, 106, 125(a) of BNS and charge sheet was filed under Sec.281 and 106 of BNS against the rider of the offending vehicle.
4. The Petitioners submit that the accident took place due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending vehicle.

It is submitted that the deceased was hale and healthy and aged about 38 years and was an agriculturist and doing dairy farming and was earning Rs.20,000/- p.m. at the time of accident and he was the sole bread earner and had good future prospects.
Due to untimely death of the deceased the Petitioners SCCH 15 5 MVC No.6459/2024 have lost love, affection and support which has caused mental agony to the petitioners.
Hence, the petitioners have claimed compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- with costs and interest at the rate of 12% p.a in the interest of justice and equity.
5. In pursuance of service of notice issued to the Respondents, Respondent No.1 remained absent and he was placed exparte.

The Respondent No.2 has filed written statement submitting as follows:
The respondent No.2 denies that they have issued insurance policy to the offending vehicle in favour of respondent No.1.
Without prejudice the liability of the respondent No.2 if any is subject to the validity of driving license and terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
The Respondent No.2 in its Objection Statement denied that the accident was caused by rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle.
The rider of the motorcycle did not have valid and effective driving license.

The age,
avocation and SCCH 15 6 MVC No.6459/2024 income of the deceased is denied.
The petition is bad for non joinder of necessary parties.
Hence, on these grounds Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.

6. Vide order dated 10.07.2025 the following issues were framed by this Tribunal :-
Issues 1) Whether the Petitioners prove that Sri. M. Eraswamy S/o Marisiddaiah died in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 29.07.2024 at about 5.00 p.m., near Banana plantation, on K.M. Doddi - Halaguru main road, Dadamalli - Antaralli, Mandya district, due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-LV-8632?
2.
Whether the Petitioners further prove that they are the legal heirs of deceased M. Eraswamy?
3) Whether the Petitioners are entitled for the compensation as prayed for?
If yes, SCCH 15 7 MVC No.6459/2024 what is the quantum and who is liable to pay ?

sentences.text: In order to substantiate the claim petition, the claimants have examined petitioner No.1 as PW1 and relied upon Ex.P1 to 15 documents.
8. Oral submissions were advanced by Ld. Counsel for parties in this case.

Having perused the records my Issue wise findings run as under:-
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative. Issue No.4 : As per the Final Order for the following :
REASONS 9. Issue No.1: Before adjudication of the Issue with respect to the compensation it is quintessential to adjudicate on the Issue of negligence.

It is the contention of the learned SCCH 15 8 MVC No.6459/2024 counsel for the petitioners that the rash and negligent riding of rider of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-LV-8632 / offending vehicle caused the accident resulting in the death of Eraswamy.

10. In this regard the petitioner No 1 has got herself examined as PW1 and in her chief examination she has deposed that on 29.07.2024 at about 5.00 p.m., deceased Eraswamy was proceeding in a motorcycle bearing Reg.KA-05-LV-8632 as a pillion rider and when they reached near Banana tree plantation, KM Doddi - Halaguru main road, at that time, rider of the offending vehicle came in a rash and negligent manner and in the process of avoiding the cow suddenly came on the road, lost control and turned to the left side, as result both rider and pillion rider fell down and sustained grievous head injuries and later succumbed to the injuries.
11.

The petitioners in support of their claim have in addition to describing the course of the accident in line with the facts mentioned in the complaint have relied upon Ex.P1 to 9 SCCH 15 9 MVC No.6459/2024 documents.

Ex.P1 is the FIR filed against the rider of the motorcycle for the offenses under Sec.281, 106, 125(a) of BNS on the basis of complaint given by PW.1 on 30.07.2024 next day of the accident and hence there is no delay in lodging the complaint.

Ex.P3 and 4 are the Spot mahazar and spot sketch which discloses the spot of the accident, said road is straight road and 18 feet road and accident has taken from north edge towards south at a distance of 17 feet and there is banana plantation about 120 feet away from the road.

The accident stated to have occurred when the cow suddenly came on the road and fact that the place is village with plantation, it can be assumed the accident occurred when the motorist went to avoid the cow and lost control over his vehicle.

Ex.P5 is the seizure mahazar of the vehicle and Ex.P6 & 7 are the inquest mahazar and PM report which elicit that husband of the petitioner No.1 succumbed to the injuries due to the impact of the accident.
Ex.P8 is the motor vehicle accident report that discloses the damages sustained to the motorcycle.

Ex.P9 charge sheet is SCCH 15 10 MVC No.6459/2024 filed after completion of investigation against the rider of the offending vehicle for the offenses under Sec.281 and 106 of BNS which discloses that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle.

Hence, these documents satisfactorily establish that the accident took place Geetha B vs Ravi H D on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104416865/
4 due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle.
12.

sentences.text: As far as the manner of the accident is concerned PW.1 is cross-examined by the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 and she has deposed that she has not seen the accident and one Puttaraju informed her about the accident and she denied that they were not wearing helmet at the time of the accident.
She has also denied that her husband was riding the motorcycle and accident has occurred due to his negligence.

Except the suggestion that the accident took place due to the negligence of the deceased himself, nothing much is elicited in the cross-examination in the cross-examination of PW.1 to prove that the accident took place due to the negligence of the SCCH 15 11 MVC No.6459/2024 deceased.
There is no material on record which suggests falsity or untruth in the oral testimony of PW.1 as to the facts and circumstances surrounding cause of the accident.
The fact that the driver of the offending vehicle has already been charge sheeted for the offenses under Sec. 281 and 106 of BNS itself is strong circumstance to support the oral testimony of PW.1.
The certified copies of FIR, charge sheet, IMV report and Spot mahazar also corroborate the oral testimony of PW.1.
In view of medical records there is no dispute regarding the death occurred in the above accident.
In view of the said discussion it is satisfactorily established that death occurred on account of rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle at the relevant time.

Hence, issue No.1 is answered in favour of the petitioner and in the 'Affirmative'.
13. Issue No.2:
It is stated in the Petition as well as in the evidence of PW.1 that the Petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioner No.2 and 3 are the sons and petitioner No.4 is the mother of the deceased Eraswamy.
To prove their relationship SCCH 15 12 MVC No.6459/2024 with the deceased, PW.1 has relied on Ex.P10 to 14 i.e., the Aadhaar cards of the deceased and petitioners.
Hence, they have a right to apply for compensation due to death of Eraswamy in road traffic accident.

14. In the case of Seema Rani & Ors. v. The Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. & Ors 2025 the Supreme Court reiterated that the major, married, and earning children of a deceased victim, as the legal representatives, have the right to apply for motor accident compensation.

entities.text: Seema Rani & Ors. v. The Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. & Ors 2025
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Reliance can also be placed on the dictum in National Insurance Company Limited v. Birender (2020), wherein it was expounded that "major married and earning sons of the deceased, being legal representatives, have a right to apply for compensation, and the Tribunal must consider the application, irrespective of whether the representatives are fully dependent on the deceased or not."

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited v. Birender (2020)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 15. The Petitioner No.1 being the wife, petitioner No.2 and SCCH 15 13 MVC No.6459/2024 3 are the sons and petitioner No.4 is the mother of the deceased, being the legal representatives of deceased Eraswamy have a right to apply for compensation.

As the Petitioners are the LRs of deceased Eraswamy and also they have proved that the death of Eraswamy has been caused by the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle, they are entitled for just compensation.
Hence I answer Issue No 2 in the Affirmative.
16. Issue No.3: Computation of compensation under the various heads is assessed as follows:
1. Loss of dependency Age factor:

In order to assess the compensation under the head of loss of dependency the age, avocation and income of the deceased needs to be Geetha B vs Ravi H D on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104416865/
5 ascertained.

sentences.text: In the present case, the age of the deceased is shown as 38 years.
Ex.P-14 is the Aadhaar card which shows that the date of birth of the deceased is 01.01.1986.
The alleged accident has taken place on SCCH 15 14 MVC No.6459/2024 29.07.2024.
Hence, by considering Ex.P14, the age of the deceased is taken as 38 years.
17. Income and avocation:
It is stated in the evidence that deceased was an agriculturist and doing dairy farming and was earning Rs.20,000/- p.m.
However in cross-examination of PW.1 she has deposed that she has not produced any documents to show deceased's avocation and income.
Hence in the absence of evidence to prove the actual income of the deceased the notional income will have to be taken into consideration.
Looking into the age of the deceased and the avocation the notional income as per the minimum wages Act it is just and proper to fix the notional income of the deceased as Rs.16,500/- per month.
Therefore, the Annual Income of the deceased would be 16,500X 12= 1,98,000/-.
Hence for the purpose of computation of claim, the annual income of the deceased is taken as Rs.1,98,000/-.

18. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of Sarla SCCH 15 15 MVC No.6459/2024 Verma v.
DTC, reported as (2009) 6 SCC 121 has established the golden principles in considering compensation in cases of death.

entities.text:
Sarla SCCH 15 15 MVC No.6459/2024 Verma v.
DTC, reported as (2009) 6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Relevant part of the judgment at paras 18- 19 is reproduced hereunder:
"18.

The criteria which are to be taken into consideration for assessing compensation in the case of death are: (i) the age of the deceased at the time of his death; (ii) the number of dependents left behind by the deceased; and (iii) the income of the deceased at the time of his death.
There will be lesser need for detailed evidence.
It will be easier for the insurance companies to settle accident claims without delay.

19. To have uniformity and consistency, the Tribunals should determine compensation in cases of death, by the following well-settled steps:
"Step 1 (Ascertaining the multiplicand) The SCCH 15 16 MVC No.6459/2024 income of the deceased per annum should be determined.
Out of the said income a deduction should be made in regard to the amount which the deceased would have spent on himself by way of personal and living expenses.

The balance, which is considered to Geetha B vs Ravi H D on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104416865/
6 be the contribution to the dependant family, constitutes the multiplicand.

entities.text: Geetha B vs Ravi H D
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Step 2 (Ascertaining the multiplier)
Having regard to the age of the deceased and period of active career, the appropriate multiplier should be selected.
This does not mean ascertaining the number of years he would have lived or worked but for the accident.
Having regard to several imponderables in life and economic factors, a Table of multipliers with reference to the age has been identified by this Court.
The multiplier should be chosen from the said Table with reference to the age of the deceased."

Moving forward with the Issue of future prospects, the Constitution Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of National Insurance Company Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi reported as (2017) 16 SCC 680, held that Future prospects are to be awarded on the basis of:
(i) The nature of the deceased's employment; and (ii) The age of the deceased.
Relying on Para 59.4 of Pranay Sethi (supra), while determining the income, an addition of 40% of actual salary to the income of the deceased towards future prospects should be made, where SCCH 15 17 MVC No.6459/2024 the deceased is permanently employed and was below the age of 40 years.
19.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi reported as (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: At the time of the death of the deceased, he was survived by his wife, sons and mother.
Hence while calculating the deductions towards the personal expenses, the number of dependents at the time of the death of the deceased is to be considered.

As per the dicta of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India where the number of dependents of family members is 4 to 6, 1/4th of the income of the deceased may be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.
20. In this Petition, the deceased was aged 38 years at the time of accident.
Hence, towards future prospects 40% of the income has to be added.
So, 40% of Rs.16,500/- comes to Rs.6,600/-.

Therefore, the income of the deceased comes to Rs.23,100/- p.m. (Rs.16,500/- + Rs.6,600/- =
Rs.23,100/-).

Further, as per the principles laid down in decision reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 (Sarla Verma and Others Vs. Delhi SCCH 15 18 MVC No.6459/2024 Transport Corporation and another) the multiplier applicable is 15.

entities.text: (2009) 6 SCC 121 (Sarla Verma and Others Vs. Delhi SCCH 15 18 MVC No.6459/2024 Transport Corporation and another)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In Sarla Verma's case, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India has pleased to hold that where the number of dependent of family members is 4 to 6, 1/4th of the income of the deceased may be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.

21. After deducting 1/4th of the income towards his personal expenses in Rs.23,100/- it comes to Rs.17,325/- (Rs.23,100/- - 5,775/-) and multiplier applied is 15, (Rs.17,325/- x 12 = 2,07,900/-,
Rs.2,07,900/- x 15 = 31,18,500/-).
Thus, the Petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.31,18,500/- towards loss of dependency.
22. Medical expenses:
The petitioners have not produced any medical bills to show any expenses incurred in the hospital.

Hence the actual medical expenses incurred for the treatment of the Geetha B vs Ravi H D on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104416865/
7 deceased or any hospital charges are taken an Nil.
23. 'Loss of Estate', Loss of Consortium' and 'Funeral Expenses' In view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme SCCH 15 19 MVC No.6459/2024 Court in Pranay Sethi (Supra), the conventional heads, namely, 'Loss of Estate', Loss of Consortium' and 'Funeral Expenses', amount of compensation is fixed as Rs. 15,000/-, Rs.40,000/- and Rs. 15,000/-, respectively with an increase of 10% after a period of 3 years.

sentences.text: It is further observed in the aforesaid Judgment amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.
The said Judgment was rendered on 30.10.2017.

By applying the said observation made in the aforesaid case, since, more than 6 years lapsed from the date of Order, the consortium fixed in the said case should be enhanced from Rs.40,000/- to Rs.48,400/-.
Further, the loss of estate and funeral expenses also extended to Rs.18,150/- each.

In view of the decision in United India Insurance Company Limited Vs Satinder Kaur Alias Satwinder Kaur and Ors. (2021) 11 SCC 780, no compensation is to be granted under the head 'Loss of Love and Affection'.

In view of the foregoing reasons and discussions, the petitioners are entitled to compensation amount of Rs.33,48,400/-.

24. Regarding rate of interest: As far as the rate of interest is concerned the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in SHRIRAM GENERAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED VS. RAJASTAN VS. SMT.
LAXMI reported in 2018 (4) AKR 808 has held that in case of motor accident claims rate of interest awarded is 6% per annum and the Hon'ble High court has been consistently granting 6% interest in Motor Vehicles Accident Claims and Compensation cases.

LAXMI reported in 2018 (4) AKR 808
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence the rate of interest is set at 6% per annum in this case.
25. Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle.
There is no dispute about the validity of the Policy at the time of the accident.
In this case, the Respondent No.1 is the owner and Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, the Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to satisfy the award amount.
However the Respondent No.2 being the insurer is liable to indemnify the Respondent No.1/insured and will have to deposit the compensation amount payable to the Petitioners.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.3 is "Partly in the Affirmative".
26. Issue No.4:
From the above discussion, I am of the opinion that the Petitioner No.1 to 4 are entitled for compensation of Rs.33,48,400/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition.

In the result, I proceed to pass the following :
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioners against the Respondents and under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.

The Petitioner No.1 to 4 are entitled for total compensation of Rs.33,48,400/- along with cost and simple interest at the SCCH 15 23 MVC No.6459/2024 rate of 6% p.a.,
from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
The Respondent No.2 being the insurer, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.

This petition emanates from the Motor Vehicle Accident dated 29.07.2024 wherein the petitioners have sought for compensation with respect to the death of Sri Eraswamy due to the impact of the accident.
2. Succinctly stated the facts germane to the lis involved in this petition are briefly summarized as follows:
opennyai_summary.facts:
It is the case of the petitioners that the petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioner No.2 and 3 are the sons and petitioner No.4 is the mother of the deceased Eraswamy who died in the Road Traffic Accident on 29.07.2024 due to the negligence of the rider of the respondent's vehicle.
Consequently, on 30.07.2024 FIR No.0129/2024 was registered with the Halagur Police station under Sec.281, 106, 125(a) of BNS and charge sheet was filed under Sec.281 and 106 of BNS against the rider of the offending vehicle.
4. The Petitioners submit that the accident took place due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending vehicle.
The Respondent No.2 has filed written statement submitting as follows:
The respondent No.2 denies that they have issued insurance policy to the offending vehicle in favour of respondent No.1.
The Respondent No.2 in its Objection Statement denied that the accident was caused by rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle.
The rider of the motorcycle did not have valid and effective driving license.
opennyai_summary.issue:
6. Vide order dated 10.07.2025 the following issues were framed by this Tribunal :-
Issues 1) Whether the Petitioners prove that Sri. M. Eraswamy S/o Marisiddaiah died in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 29.07.2024 at about 5.00 p.m., near Banana plantation, on K.M. Doddi - Halaguru main road, Dadamalli - Antaralli, Mandya district, due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-LV-8632?
2.
Whether the Petitioners further prove that they are the legal heirs of deceased M. Eraswamy?
3) Whether the Petitioners are entitled for the compensation as prayed for?
If yes, SCCH 15 7 MVC No.6459/2024 what is the quantum and who is liable to pay ?
opennyai_summary.arguments:
It is the contention of the learned SCCH 15 8 MVC No.6459/2024 counsel for the petitioners that the rash and negligent riding of rider of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-LV-8632 / offending vehicle caused the accident resulting in the death of Eraswamy.
10. In this regard the petitioner No 1 has got herself examined as PW1 and in her chief examination she has deposed that on 29.07.2024 at about 5.00 p.m., deceased Eraswamy was proceeding in a motorcycle bearing Reg.KA-05-LV-8632 as a pillion rider and when they reached near Banana tree plantation, KM Doddi - Halaguru main road, at that time, rider of the offending vehicle came in a rash and negligent manner and in the process of avoiding the cow suddenly came on the road, lost control and turned to the left side, as result both rider and pillion rider fell down and sustained grievous head injuries and later succumbed to the injuries.
11.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Ex.P1 is the FIR filed against the rider of the motorcycle for the offenses under Sec.281, 106, 125(a) of BNS on the basis of complaint given by PW.1 on 30.07.2024 next day of the accident and hence there is no delay in lodging the complaint.
Hence, these documents satisfactorily establish that the accident took place Geetha B vs Ravi H D on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104416865/
4 due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle.
12.
There is no material on record which suggests falsity or untruth in the oral testimony of PW.1 as to the facts and circumstances surrounding cause of the accident.
The fact that the driver of the offending vehicle has already been charge sheeted for the offenses under Sec. 281 and 106 of BNS itself is strong circumstance to support the oral testimony of PW.1.
The certified copies of FIR, charge sheet, IMV report and Spot mahazar also corroborate the oral testimony of PW.1.
In view of medical records there is no dispute regarding the death occurred in the above accident.
In view of the said discussion it is satisfactorily established that death occurred on account of rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
Looking into the age of the deceased and the avocation the notional income as per the minimum wages Act it is just and proper to fix the notional income of the deceased as Rs.16,500/- per month.
Hence for the purpose of computation of claim, the annual income of the deceased is taken as Rs.1,98,000/-.
18. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of Sarla SCCH 15 15 MVC No.6459/2024 Verma v.
DTC, reported as (2009) 6 SCC 121 has established the golden principles in considering compensation in cases of death.
Moving forward with the Issue of future prospects, the Constitution Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of National Insurance Company Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi reported as (2017) 16 SCC 680, held that Future prospects are to be awarded on the basis of:
(i) The nature of the deceased's employment; and (ii) The age of the deceased.
Relying on Para 59.4 of Pranay Sethi (supra), while determining the income, an addition of 40% of actual salary to the income of the deceased towards future prospects should be made, where SCCH 15 17 MVC No.6459/2024 the deceased is permanently employed and was below the age of 40 years.
19.
At the time of the death of the deceased, he was survived by his wife, sons and mother.
Hence while calculating the deductions towards the personal expenses, the number of dependents at the time of the death of the deceased is to be considered.
Hence, towards future prospects 40% of the income has to be added.
Further, as per the principles laid down in decision reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 (Sarla Verma and Others Vs. Delhi SCCH 15 18 MVC No.6459/2024 Transport Corporation and another) the multiplier applicable is 15.
In view of the decision in United India Insurance Company Limited Vs Satinder Kaur Alias Satwinder Kaur and Ors. (2021) 11 SCC 780, no compensation is to be granted under the head 'Loss of Love and Affection'.

Thus, the Petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.31,18,500/- towards loss of dependency.
It is further observed in the aforesaid Judgment amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.
The said Judgment was rendered on 30.10.2017.
By applying the said observation made in the aforesaid case, since, more than 6 years lapsed from the date of Order, the consortium fixed in the said case should be enhanced from Rs.40,000/- to Rs.48,400/-.
Further, the loss of estate and funeral expenses also extended to Rs.18,150/- each.
In light of the above discussion, the claimants are awarded compensation as follows:

26. Issue No.4:
From the above discussion, I am of the opinion that the Petitioner No.1 to 4 are entitled for compensation of Rs.33,48,400/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition.
In the result, I proceed to pass the following :
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioners against the Respondents and under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Petitioner No.1 to 4 are entitled for total compensation of Rs.33,48,400/- along with cost and simple interest at the SCCH 15 23 MVC No.6459/2024 rate of 6% p.a.,
from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
The Respondent No.2 being the insurer, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.
Geetha B vs Ravi H D on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104416865/
9
The compensation amount awarded to the Petitioner No.1 to 4 are apportioned among them are as shown below:
1) 50% to the Petitioner No.1 2) 20% each to the Petitioner No.2 and 3 3) 10% to the petitioner No.4
After deposit of the Award amount and interest by the Respondent No.2, out of the amount awarded to the Petitioner No.1, 50% of the award amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner No.1 by way of SCCH 15 24 MVC No.6459/2024 E-payment and after her proper identification and the remaining 50%
of the award amount shall be kept in Fixed deposit in the name of Petitioner No.1 in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank for a period of 3 years of her choice.
The entire amount awarded to the Petitioner No.2 and 3 shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in their names in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank till they attains age of majority.
Further, the natural guardian/mother of the minor Petitioner No.1 and 2 is permitted to withdraw the interest on the said Fixed deposit periodically to the best interest of the minor Petitioners.
Since, the amount awarded to the Petitioner No.4 is meager, the entire amount awarded to Petitioner No.4 shall be released to her by way of E- payment and after her proper identification.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
